text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Cross-region routing anomaly detected for region 'eu-west-1' - elevated 5xx and latency deviation. Metric: 5xx_rate=4.1% (baseline 0.2%), p50 latency 420ms (baseline 70ms). Trigger: routing-policy/latency-steering-v2. Investigation recommended. https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/CR-2129876543

morgan: paging @priya (oncall) — can you take? Looks like something in the recent routing policy rollout.

priya: on it. ACKed pager. grabbing logs and route state now. ETA 2m.

morgan: quick context: we rolled out `latency-steering-v2` 35m ago to improve EU latency. Early signal shows uneven pin propagation at edge caches -> some EU customer requests are being routed to us-west which doesn't have the matching gateway cert/model variant, causing TLS/5xx.

priya: running check against route cache and policy state:```bash
$ rtrctl inspect --policy latency-steering-v2 --regions eu-west-1,us-west-1
policy: latency-steering-v2
edges: eu-west-1: active (pins=87, pending=3)
       us-west-1: active (pins=12, pending=45)
inconsistencies: cache-miss on CDN edge id cdn-euw-23 -> fallback to us-west-1
```Seeing pending pins not applied on a subset of edges (cdn-euw-2*, cdn-euw-23).

sam: seeing matching spike in origin errors: TLS handshake fail + 503 from legacy gateway when requests hit us-west. Suspect SNI mismatch because the model variants in us-west are different build (v1 vs v2).

lin: can we quickly roll back policy to previous version (latency-steering-v1) or flip to `region-pin-strict` to enforce hard pinning while we debug? Rolling back would be quickest.

priya: initiating rollback now via control-plane API:```bash
$ curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/v1/policies/latency-steering-v2/rollback 
  -d '{"target_version":"3"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```API response: `{"status":"ok","applied_version":"3","change_id":"chg-2129876557"}`

incident-bot: Change chg-2129876557 applied to policy latency-steering-v2. Notifying edge controllers to re-evaluate pins.

priya: triggering cache flush for affected edges and lowering DNS TTL for region endpoints to speed re-propagation:```bash
$ cdnctl flush --edge cdn-euw-23,cdn-euw-2*
$ dnsctl set-ttl api.euw.redwood.ai 60
```flush started, dns TTL updated.

morgan: rolling rollback + cache flush applied. Monitoring. Also increase retry budget for clients to reduce user visible failures while pins settle.

maya: customer impact update: from metrics and error telemetry - ~31 customers had degraded responses in last 12m, majority EU-based. Estimated affected requests ~120k, SLO risk window ~3-10m. Notifying ops-contacts for high-touch customers. Status page draft: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/CR-2129876543

sam: verifying health after rollback: p50 back to ~85ms in eu-west, 5xx down to 0.3%. A few edges still catching up but trend is good.

lin: leaving a short-term mitigation note in runbook: if latency-steering-v2 shows pending pins > 5 on any EU edge after rollout -> pause rollout and escalate to infra. Also add a preflight to check edge cache version compatibility with new policy.

priya: handoff: I'll continue monitoring for 15m then hand to @sam (night oncall). Action items: (1) infra to investigate why edge controller queued pins but didn't apply (ticket INF-CR-212987), (2) release team to ensure variant parity across regions, (3) ops to confirm customers notified.

morgan: thanks team. Good quick mitigation. Sam, you're oncall for follow-ups — ping if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

sam: got it, picking up handoff. I'll keep watch and update status page if anything new.

incident-bot: Incident CR-2129876543 transitioned to "mitigated" (temporary rollback applied). Follow-up tasks recorded: INF-CR-212987, REL-CR-212988, OPS-CR-212989.

morgan: final note - schedule a postmortem to review rollout gating and edge cache TTL behaviour. Suggest 60m blameless review in infra channel tomorrow.

priya: thanks all. closing urgent loop, will update ticket with exact timeline and logs.
